newsitem.title: USA: US Gulf Coast prods rise with NYMEX, diffs steady.
newsitem.headline: US Gulf Coast prods rise with NYMEX, diffs steady.

text.p: U.S. Gulf Coast refined products prices rose with higher futures markets late Tuesday, while afternoon differentials were little changed as traders awaited weekly inventory data, traders said.
Activity was light, with traders bowing out ahead of American Petroleum Institute's weekly report, a key indicator of supply and demand in U.S. energy markets.

NYMEX markets, the basis for Midcontinent spot prices, rose from the morning, although May unleaded gasoline settled 0.06 cents a gallon lower. Like gasoline, heating oil gained ground from the early morning and settled 0.18 cents higher.

Gasoline stocks confounded forecasts, rising a huge 3.6-million-barrels last week, according to API. The rise in stocks, predicted by some analysts, may have resulted when floods in the U.S. heartland put a dent in driving demand.
Buyers of regular unleaded gasoline in Group Three were willing to pay 0.50 cents a gallon under May NYMEX unleaded futures, or the same level as Tuesday morning.
Differentials for premium gasoline in the Group edged up 0.25 cents from early talk, topping the screen by 3.75 to 4.00 cents.
Chicago unleaded meanwhile pared gains registered Monday, which traders linked to maintenance outages at a number of refineries in the region.
Prompt Chicago premium was pegged at 5.25 cents over regular unleaded, off a slight 0.25 cents from the morning.
Also in the Group, traders said some players were beginning to roll their prompt low sulphur diesel positions to any month.
Prompt material fetched about 6.25 cents over May NYMEX heat, 0.25 cents lower than earlier, with any month barrels keeping pace. They were talked at a sharply backwardated 5.25 cents.
